title: Book 10 opens: still on holy tent furnishings; word clear but not enough
english: ON ADORATION AND WORSHIP IN SPIRIT AND TRUTH — BOOK TEN. Concerning the same things still, and concerning the things in the holy tent. Is the word clear to you then, O Palladius, and sufficient, which we have made upon the holy tent and the things in it?
notes_covered: Cyril asks if prior word suffices
translator_notes: §1 ends into Palladius reply in §2; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Pitch tent on new-moon first month; Moses builds Church-type; Jesus with Moses vs Amalek
english: Palladius: Clear indeed very well, yet sufficient least of all.

Cyril: Do you wish then that we most eagerly cross again unto that which seems to have been left behind in the narrations upon it? For you think somehow, according to what is likely, that the clarifying word must also be brought alongside, in what manner it has been raised for us, and when and how the righteous-ordinances and laws in it have been composed, and inauguration and sanctification and judgment.
Palladius: Speak then again the things upon each; for you think uprightly.

Cyril: So then I will speak. And you in turn be forgiving, having thought through the complete difficulty of the contemplations, and if somewhere I should chance to say something of the things that have missed exactness and have wandered out from the needed word, reshape and readjust. For I will make you a fellow-taker and helper of my own words.
Palladius: Go trusting God.

Cyril: So then when the works of the holy tent had been thoroughly completed, and indeed also each of the things in it wisely and artfully finished toward the beauty shown on the mountain, the Lord spoke toward Moses, saying, ‘On day one of the month the first, at new-moon, you will set up the tent of the testimony.’ And after other things again: ‘And it came to be,’ he says, ‘in the month the first, in the second year of their going out from Egypt, at new-moon, the tent was stood, and Moses set up the tent.’ So then the ancient tent of the Church thought in Christ has been raised according to what seemed good to God, showing the types very well upon itself. And let us busy ourselves, if it seems good, with the causes of its having been raised rather through Moses, Jesus the son of Nun being silent for the present, though always standing beside all-excellent Moses, and leaping up together upon the mountain Sinai, and also making war and leading out against Amalek through Moses’ voice. For he said somewhere toward him, ‘Choose for yourself strong men, and going out draw up against Amalek tomorrow.’ And he drew up, and he has conquered. What then is the word of this—is it not worthy to examine?
Palladius: Very much so.

Cyril: So then if someone should choose to exact the word of the mystery upon each of the things done as far as possible, marveling he will say, ‘O depth of wealth and wisdom and knowledge of God!’ For observe how subtle and necessary is the mind upon each: for when all-divine Moses runs up unto the mountain, Jesus goes up together; for the Father is not otherwise approachable, except through Son. For it is also true, if it should be said: ‘No one comes toward the Father, except through me.’ In Christ therefore also for the saints themselves is the approach; and no one would be able, as unto a mountain, to leap up unto some high and surpassing contemplation, nor would anyone, I think, come near God, according to manner clearly
notes_covered: Jesus of Nun with Moses / Amalek
translator_notes: Ends mid-word/phrase into §3 συναφείας; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Emmanuel makes rough ways passable; Moses’ pedagogy builds Church; one saving day
english: Cyril: …of joining, of the way of life in spirit and sanctification, unless Emmanuel also is present with him, and sets the things unreachable for humans as passable and horse-ridden. And this, I think, is what has been said through Isaiah’s voice, ‘Every ravine will be filled, and every mountain and hill will be lowered, and all the crooked will be unto a straight, and the rough unto smooth roads.’ For in Christ for us also the steep are smooth, and the rough is passable; and bare and level are the hard-to-travel. For also, as the prophet himself says somewhere again, ‘A road of pious ones. It has become straight, and prepared is the road of the pious.’ So then necessarily Jesus goes up together with all-divine Moses. For the Father is approachable, as I said, through Son, and he himself is the mediator, joining us through himself, and carrying us up into the heights beyond nature. And he had drawn up with chosen men, and was conquering Amalek. For Christ, having chosen the saints, of whom the all-divine disciples have become firstfruit, has conquered the ruler of this age; and Moses was the one commanding; for the Son has come to be under law, though existing as lawgiver as God. And the time of the battle-array was not being practiced according to that very day on which Moses’ words came to be, but unto the tomorrow—that is, unto a putting-off of another time. For the law foretold the things that would be, and has a bright narration of the Savior’s achievements, if it should be thought spiritually. In this way then, as I myself somehow think, Moses also raised the holy tent. For the pedagogy through law unto the constitution of the Church is not unhelpful. For it pedagogues unto Christ, who is the head of the Church, and the whole constitution, pillar and foundation of the truth, according to what has been written. And indeed Christ has addressed Jews: ‘If you were believing Moses, you would also believe me; for concerning me that one wrote.’ So then Moses also builds—that is, the pedagogy through law—the Church of Christ, still showing beforehand as in shadows the mystery upon it. And Moses’ person sometimes presents the law through him, according at least to what has been uprightly said in Gospel parables, ‘They have Moses and the prophets.’
Palladius: You have spoken uprightly.

Cyril: And what again would the needing on day one wish to signify, and indeed also the new-moon of the month the first, and the needing for the holy tent to be pegged in the second year—come then let us say, tracking the true, and what seems to hold most excellently for those who will meet it. For day the one shows beforehand for us the much-prayed and saving time, according to which the Only-begotten having become human acquired those upon the earth for God and Father by the death of his own flesh. And one is the time of this of all; for having died once, he no longer dies; death will no longer lord over him, according to the Scriptures; for we will not still expect the Son to die for us ourselves and for the spirits in Hades, nor yet
translator_notes: Continues §2 mid-cut συναφείας; ends mid into §4 firstfruit a second time.

title: One acceptable day; apostles build Gentile Church; Christ many-formed in believers
english: Cyril: …to become firstfruit of those who have fallen asleep a second time. For if death will not be, how would resurrection also come to be? So then it is not to speak falsely when saying that one is the time of this, as I said just now, and day one, of which the prophet also made mention saying as from God’s person, ‘In an acceptable time I heard you, and in a day of salvation I helped you.’ And all-divine Paul also writes, ‘Behold now an acceptable time, behold now a day of salvation,’ according to which Christ lived again from dead ones, having dissolved the unsmiling power of death, when also he was setting the holy apostles as somehow builders and spiritual craftsmen of the Church from nations, saying, ‘Going, disciple all the nations, baptizing them unto the name of the Father and of the Son and of the holy Spirit, teaching them to keep all things, as many as I commanded you; and behold I am with you all the days until the completion of the age.’ For do you not say that this is the constitution of the Church?
Palladius: What then do you say?

Cyril: The faith handed over through the holy mystagogues, and the way of life proclaimed—I mean the one in Christ—and the union toward God through holy baptism, through participation of the holy Spirit. For thus Paul was addressing us saying, ‘And you as living stones are being built up a spiritual house, unto a holy temple, unto a dwelling of God in Spirit.’ For long ago Christ was being pre-formed as in differing vessels in the holy tent—as golden censer, as ark, as lampstand, and indeed also as table, and the things in it; and each, I think, of those who have believed, according at least to the present time, is named house and temple of God, having Christ dwelling within. For he dwells in our hearts through the faith, as has been written, existing one and the same according to nature, even if he should be thought with flesh. ‘For one God the Father, from whom are all things, and one Lord Jesus Christ, through whom are all things,’ having upon himself the as-it-were many-formed through the differing properties of the godhead, and being thought differently. For he is in us as Word of God, and wisdom, and light, and life, and the living bread also from heaven.
Palladius: I have understood what you say.

Cyril: So then the time of the becoming-human for us, and the thrice-longed day of the resurrection from dead ones, was being typed beforehand long ago through God’s saying, On day one you will set up the tent. And the, And at new-moon of the month the first, one would see as usefully and necessarily brought alongside, O Palladius. For just as beginning of a month is the first of days in it—that is, the new-moon—so also somehow a beginning of a new age, and a first-entrance of newness of times, is the time of the sojourn. ‘For a new creation in Christ; the ancient things have passed.’ And as it were the age after this shines up for us, now still seen as in hopes, but then also about to be present
translator_notes: Ends mid-sentence into §5 truly when Christ shines again.

title: Spring new-moon = Gentile Church; second year after law; unshaken tents of Jerusalem
english: Cyril: …truly, when Christ should shine upon us again with the holy angels in the glory of the Father, about to take alongside himself those who have chosen to walk in newness of life, and who have enriched in endurance the most conspicuous beauty of the Gospel way of life, and bringing them into the glory and kingdom long expected. And that a new creation and as it were a new sprout of times and matters belongs to those in Christ, the riddle of the first month would show very well, according to which soft and newly-appearing grasses are on earth, and sprouting-again of plants, and the many-formed beauty of flowers in meadows is shown, of spring laughing fragrance; for somehow in such a time Christ has called the Church from nations, saying thus, ‘Rise, come, my neighbor, my fair one, my dove, because behold the winter has gone away, the rain has gone away, it has traveled in it; the flowers have been seen on the earth; time of cutting has arrived.’ For human nature has sprouted again, as some plant, having been withered by death, both through the transgression in Adam and through the sin that tyrannized over all of us. And I hear Christ saying also through one of the holy prophets, ‘I myself who speak am present, as an hour upon the mountains.’ For what spring works in mountains and thickets, crowning the plants with new sprout, this also our Savior’s presence has fulfilled upon us, having come to be according to times, as in a second year, and not at least in the first time, according to which the law was, and the chorus of the prophets, and according to which death was ruling. For it has reigned from Adam and until Moses. So then as in a second year—that is, as in a time after the first, according to which the law was—the Church from nations has shone up, having Christ as inmate, the end of the prophets and of the law. Does the word seem to you to shoot through toward the straight and true?
Palladius: Altogether so.

Cyril: And I myself think that the more true tent has been announced beforehand for us through Isaiah’s voice, saying as toward each of those called in faith unto righteousness, ‘Your eyes will see Jerusalem, rich cities, tents which will not be shaken, nor will the pegs of its tent be moved; nor will its ropes be torn apart unto the age-long time.’ For the Church is God’s city, of which also all-divine David made mention saying, ‘Glorious things have been spoken concerning you, the city of God.’ For this is rich, and adorned with the gifts from above and from heaven, and having an unbreakable standing in firmness, a seating and remaining. ‘For gates of Hades will not overpower it,’ according to the Savior’s voice.
Palladius: You think most uprightly and fittingly.
Cyril: And when the tent has been raised, that it is fitting for the things in it to lie in order, and not poured-out and carelessly, the Master God of all teaches saying:
notes_covered: Song 2:10-12 spring call to Gentile Church
translator_notes: Ends at God’s command quote opening §6.

title: Place vessels; veil of four pillars; Holies / Holies of holies; laver between
english: Cyril: ‘And you will set the ark of the testimony, and you will cover the ark with the veil. And you will bring in the table, and you will set forth its setting-forth. And you will bring in the lampstand, and you will set on its lamps. And you will set the golden altar, unto incense opposite the ark. And you will set a covering of veil upon the door of the tent of the testimony, and you will set the altar of the fruit-offerings beside the doors of the tent of the testimony. And you will put around the tent, and you will put around all its things in a circle.’ But it is possible in these to see the holy vessels brought into the holy tent; yet not still also clearly the place fitting and allotted to each. Do you wish then that from the commands upon the tent we gather a subtle and exact knowledge of such things?
Palladius: As most pleasantly.

Cyril: So then God said toward holy Moses: ‘And you will make a veil from hyacinth and purple, and spun scarlet, and twined linen; a woven work you will make it Cherubim. And you will set it upon four undecaying pillars gilded with gold. And their capitals gold, and their bases four silver. And you will set the veil upon the pillars, and you will bring in there inward of the veil the ark of the testimony. And the veil will divide for you between the Holy, and between the Holy of holies. You will cover with the veil the ark of the testimony in the Holy of holies. And you will set the table outside the veil, and the lampstand opposite the table upon the part of the tent toward south. And you will set the table upon the part of the tent toward north. And you will make a curtain for the door of the tent from hyacinth and purple, and spun scarlet, and spun linen, a work of an embroiderer. And you will make for the veil five pillars, and you will gild them with gold; and their capitals gold, and you will cast for them five bronze bases.’ And these things concerning these. And concerning the laver he somehow says thus: ‘Make a bronze laver, and a base for it bronze so as to wash, and you will set it between the tent of the testimony, and between the altar.’ Is the word upon each clear to you?
Palladius: Not at all; for I have been at a loss, know; and what the matter is, I am not able to say.

Cyril: So then upon each of the sayings set forth, having seized what finishes unto the contemplation upon them, I will make the narration clear and most distinct, as I am able. For the holy tent has been raised, O Palladius, according to the desert, as in a double placing and form. And one was the innermost; and its name, the Holies of holies. And as somehow a first-entrance and around it the first, the so-called Holies. And into the innermost tent the ark was set away, having upon four golden pillars a hanging made artfully from hyacinth and purple, and spun scarlet, and twined linen. Having
notes_covered: Exod 30 laver between tent and altar
translator_notes: Ends mid-sentence Εἰρηκότες into §7; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Veil = Christ’s flesh; four pillars = evangelists; Word hidden until resurrection
english: Cyril: …spoken already, and, as I myself somehow think, sufficiently the things upon the linen and the purple, and the spun scarlet, and indeed also hyacinth, we will push aside the same-speaking; yet that at least we will say for the present: The veil upon four golden pillars, whose bases are silver, was then hinting the mystery of Christ. For what? Did not wise Paul also name for us Christ’s body a veil, saying thus, ‘Which he inaugurated for us a fresh and living way through the veil, that is, of his flesh’?
Palladius: You have spoken uprightly.

Cyril: Observe then as in shadows and riddles, that being God and from God Father according to nature the Word has come to be as in a golden and undecaying ark, the temple from Virgin; for undecaying and honored is Christ’s body; and he was all but also being hidden as in an order of a veil, having taken the flesh; and we say the Word from God is hidden, not as having been limited in a small body; for everywhere and in all things is the Son; but by escaping notice economically, and enduring the time of the showing-forth. And the time of showing-forth unto all is the living-again from dead ones. For before the honored cross, he was ordering the holy disciples that they not make him apparent. For it has been written thus. And after at least living again having suffered the death, ‘Going,’ he says, ‘disciple all the nations, baptizing them unto the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the holy Spirit.’ So then the veil was hanging upon the pillars, covering within the ark, and it would be a type of Christ, being raised high by the proclamations of the holy evangelists, and being seen in glory of godhead by those in the holy tent—that is, the Church. And four are the pillars, golden and silver-around; and equal in number to them are the evangelists, bright and honored. So then the ark was lying, and from above downward the veil was extending, the one from linen and purple and the others, and it was making it not visible. And from above the veil and of the Cherubim unto right and left, God was naming, showing that he is also beyond every creation; and also all the uppermost of the rational ones—that is, the Seraphim—sit under the divine and ineffable glory, and escorting the Son himself, even if he has become flesh, and as somehow in a lowering of the equality toward the Father, according as he has been born human. Therefore also he himself was saying: ‘My Father is greater than I.’ And being equal according to nature to the one who has begotten, he says the coming-to-be in lesser things through only the human. On account of this also in the holy tent, in a circle of the veil, the Cherubim, and they themselves escorting the Son as God. And indeed also from above the veil itself, which was unto a type of Christ, God is thought. ‘And I will be known,’ he says, ‘from there, and I will speak to you.’ For beyond every creation is the Father, and of Emmanuel himself, not according as he is thought and is God; for he is equal according to all things to God; but as far as
translator_notes: Continues §6 Εἰρηκότες; ends mid into §8 slave-form measure.

title: Golden altar fragrance; lampstand south Jews / table north Gentiles
english: Cyril: …he has come unto a slave’s form, and unto a measure of humanity.
Palladius: How subtle the word and deep.
Cyril: Yet it comes not away from the aim.
Palladius: I agree.

Cyril: And with the ark holding thus, ‘And you will set,’ he says, ‘the golden altar unto incense opposite the ark.’ And that Christ is the golden altar, I think has been said sufficiently for us. Yet it has been set opposite the ark, upon which is the veil, and in a circle the Seraphim, and higher God, as somehow receiving the incomparable fragrance of Emmanuel. For he did not do sin, nor was deceit found in his mouth, as has been written; therefore also he himself was saying, ‘The Father loves the Son.’ And we ourselves also are acceptable to God, fragrant with Christ’s ointment. And Paul will also confirm writing: ‘And to God thanks who always triumphs us in the Christ, and who manifests the smell of his knowledge through us, because we are Christ’s fragrance to God.’
Palladius: You have spoken uprightly.

Cyril: Let us think then exactly, casting the eye into the things written, that the ark has been seated in the flank of the holy tent toward southwest and west; and opposite it the golden altar, in the place toward ray. For dawn and setting have been filled with the Christ, and north and south. And indeed a place for the lampstand, the southern things of the tent; and for the table, the things toward north. And that through both the Christ is signified, a long word has already shown beforehand for us; for that Christ is light, the lampstand makes clear; and that life and living bread, the table and the things in it. Yet think that, and observe the mystery: for most southern is the country of the Jews, and more northern again that of the nations. So then from the placing of both—I mean of the lampstand and of the table—it will somehow remain for those who wish to think very well, that to the Jews Christ shone light, and among them he was proclaiming, ‘I am the light.’ For he has been sent unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel. And, ‘Theirs are the promises,’ according to the Scriptures. And since they did not accept the light of the truth, he has become for the nations life and bread from heaven; and not apart from light the nations; and this also you would learn, the light of the lampstand extending also unto the northern things of the tent. And with the holy tent being most narrow, nothing unlikely that the lampstand seems all but also to have been set beside the table, even if it should have the southern place. And the type also shows for us otherwise, that when divine light shines out those worthy would be able to share Christ, as living and true bread. And the nations have become joint-body and joint-sharers of Christ. And all-divine Paul writes again: And joint-body and joint-sharers have
notes_covered: lampstand south = Jews light; table north = Gentiles bread
translator_notes: Ends mid γέγονε into §9; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Five door pillars = fifth-age teachers; law altar at entrance; baptism laver mid-court
english: Cyril: …become the nations of light, clearly of the intelligible, being filled up additionally ‘while day is shining through, and Phosphoros rising according to mind,’ for one of the Savior’s disciples has said. And with placing and construction of the things in the Holies of holies holding thus, he has ordered a curtain, or veil, to come to be from hyacinth and purple, and spun scarlet, and twined linen; and this he was saying must necessarily be stretched around the entrances of the tent, being hung upon five golden pillars, whose bases are bronze. And he names curtain the hanging-around of the door, on account, I think, of being drawn back with fine rings when the entrance is pierced; and again being drawn against and widened of the doors, to hide the Holies. And five are the pillars, golden and bronze-around, typing beforehand the teachers and leaders of the Churches as in a fifth time, according to which Christ’s presence came to be; who, cutting-straight the word of the truth, are honored as gold, and well-sounding thus as bronze. ‘For unto all the earth their sound has gone out, and unto the ends of the inhabited world their words’; who also through artful and God-breathed mystagogy widen as it were the entrances for those wishing to run into the Holies of holies. So then the Holies of holies—that is, the more inward tent—was being covered with the veil. And at once the first tent also had been fixed beside and fitted to the second, having the altar of the fruit-offerings, in which every approach through bloods was being finished, and cakes and frankincenses, and every sacrifice and drink-offering, and indeed beside the altar also the bronze laver. And a place again for the altar beside the doors of the tent—clear that of the more outward; and for the laver, the most middle of the tent.
Palladius: And what again would the careful-watching be thought?

Cyril: Exact, O Palladius, is the holy Letter, and altogether nothing random in it. For see how the riddle has shown for us the law pedagoguing unto Christ. For the altar of the worship according to law has been set beside the very entrances unto the Holies of holies. For the law carries us off only barely unto beginnings of the mysteries of Christ, and somehow beside the first entrances of exact knowledge upon him; and it brings in in no way unto the Holies of holies—that is, unto the more inward tent, in which Christ is many-formed, as Word of God, as light, as living bread, as smell of fragrance to God and Father. For would you not say that elements and beginnings of the oracles of God were the pre-practice of the worship according to law?
Palladius: True.
Cyril: And that the law has perfected nothing, ‘For impossible for blood of bulls and goats to take away
notes_covered: five pillars = teachers of fifth age / Church leaders
law altar at doors = pedagogy only to beginnings
translator_notes: Ends mid ἁμαρτίας into §10; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Laver = baptism; outer veil hides law; Paul on two tents / two covenants
english: Cyril: …sins,’ you would learn at once, and very without toil, having also thought through the need of the laver. For it was lying in the middle of the first tent bright and conspicuous, washing beforehand with water those running into the Holies of holies. For the law upon this had been set for the priests. So then also the seeming fullness in law is incomplete, hinting the cleansing through holy baptism, which washes out the holy race—I mean that of those justified in faith—to whom also the all-divine disciple has addressed saying, ‘But you a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people unto acquisition, that you may announce the excellences of the one who called us from darkness unto his marvelous light.’ And one must know that also upon the door of the outer tent a veil had been stretched around, so that the Holies might not be bare and apparent to those from outside—that is, the first tent, in which is the altar in law—the type again making clear, I think, that not even the law itself is apparent to those who happen by. For it has a covering, the letter, and has somehow been covered and veiled with the unclarity as in shadows.
Palladius: Thus it holds.

Cyril: So then in the first tent laver was lying and altar; and in the second and innermost, the ark and the lampstand; and indeed also the golden censer, upon which the fine incense, and table and breads. And all-divine Paul also makes mention of a golden jar having the manna. And indeed he also names for us Aaron’s rod, which he says has also been set away in the Holies of holies, as being well-versed in the holy Letters, and having known that especially the things oracled according to times, and ordered to blessed Moses from God. And he knows also table and lampstand being in the first tent. And he writes thus concerning the two covenants, ‘In saying new, he has made the first old. And what is being made old and aging is near disappearance. So then the first also had righteous-ordinances of worship, and the worldly holy; for a tent was constructed the first, in which both the lampstand and the table, and the setting-forth of the breads, which is called holy. And after the second veil a tent, the one called Holies of holies, having a golden censer, and the ark of the covenant covered round from everywhere with gold, in which a golden jar having the manna, and Aaron’s rod that sprouted, and the tablets of the covenant. And above it Cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy-seat,’ concerning which it is not now to speak part by part.
Palladius: So then if someone should choose to be fond of seeking, and should say the causes of the whole construction must be spoken, what word would come to be from us?
Cyril: That, O Palladius, some things before the construction of the holy tent, and some after this, he has ordered to come to be. For in the Exodus even
translator_notes: Ends mid-sentence into §11 Exodus construction order.
